item.title: Linux: The Foundation of Modern DevOps
item.description:
Linux: The Foundation of Modern DevOps

Linux powers nearly everything on the Internet.

Whether you browse a website, stream a movie, deploy an application, or use cloud services, chances are Linux is running somewhere in the background.

If you want to become a DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), Platform Engineer, or Backend Developer, Linux is the first skill you should master.

This guide explains Linux from the ground up with practical examples and projects.

item.title: Essential Linux Mint Guides: Unlocking Encrypted Drives & Enabling Edge Copilot
item.description:
Navigating Linux Mint often comes with two common scenarios: managing secure, encrypted storage and customizing software features that aren’t enabled out of the box. Below is a comprehensive guide covering how to seamlessly access LUKS-encrypted SSDs and how to forcibly enable the Microsoft Edge Copilot sidebar using a simple custom script.

Guide 1: How to Open an Encrypted SSD in Linux Mint

Linux Mint relies on LUKS (Linux Unified Key Setup) as its standard disk encryption specification. Accessing your encrypted SSD can be handled via the graphical user interface (GUI) for ease of use or through the terminal for manual control and troubleshooting.

item.title: Optimizing Android from Linux: The Ultimate Power User Guide
item.description:
Optimizing Android from Linux: The Ultimate Power User Guide

While mainstream operating systems rely on heavy, GUI-based “one-click optimizer” utility software—which often turns out to be adware or placebo tools—Linux users have direct, granular control over their Android devices. Because Android is built on top of the Linux kernel, using a Linux desktop to manage and optimize an Android phone is a natural fit.

This guide explores the most effective ways to debloat, optimize, control, and sync your Android device directly from a Linux environment.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to AI-Assisted Coding on Linux Mint: Claude Code, OpenCode, VS Code, and VSCodium
item.description:
Agentic AI tools are transforming how developers write, refactor, and debug software directly from their terminals and IDEs. If you are running Linux Mint and looking to build a clean, powerful, privacy-respecting AI development environment, this comprehensive guide walks through everything you need to know—from setting up Anthropic’s Claude Code and the open-source OpenCode CLI to choosing and configuring your code editor.

1. What is Claude Code?

Claude Code is Anthropic’s agentic AI coding tool designed specifically for terminal-first workflows. Unlike standard chat interfaces where you copy and paste snippets back and forth, Claude Code operates directly within your local workspace environment.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Managing Swap Space and Swappiness in Linux Mint
item.description:
The Ultimate Guide to Managing Swap Space and Swappiness in Linux Mint

If your system runs low on physical RAM, Linux utilizes Swap memory as a safety net. Swap acts as a extension of your system’s RAM by allocating space on your storage drive (SSD or HDD). When physical memory is saturated, the kernel offloads inactive memory pages into swap, keeping your desktop responsive and preventing application crashes caused by Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors.

item.title: Troubleshooting Linux Boot Failures and Optimizing Linux Mint Performance
item.description:
Dealing with boot errors can be daunting, but Linux gives you full control to inspect, repair, and optimize your system. In this comprehensive guide, we cover how to fix missing EFI bootloaders, format and rebuild GRUB from scratch using live environment tools, and squeeze maximum performance out of Linux Mint.

Part 1: Resolving the “failed to open /efi/ubuntu not found” Error

When your system fails to boot and displays the error failed to open /efi/ubuntu not found, it means the UEFI firmware or GRUB bootloader cannot locate the necessary EFI binaries to start the OS. This typically occurs after major Windows updates in dual-boot setups, disk partition changes, or corrupted EFI filesystems.
